claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily dependent on luck and RNG rather than skill.

citations.review_text: I’m giving it a 4/10, and even that feels generous. Dota Underlords has a solid autobattler core with decent unit synergy and occasional strategic depth, but balance issues and RNG swings dominate most matches. Games often feel decided by early luck rather than skill, and pacing stalls in the mid‑game. The meta shifts slowly, and matchmaking can pair you against disproportionate comps. It’s functional and has moments of fun, but inconsistent mechanics and luck dependency make it hard to recommend.

Dota Underlords is like chess—if chess had explosions, gambling, and a mysterious dead crime boss named Momma Eeb. You’ll spend hours building the perfect team, only to get destroyed by some guy who accidentally stacked six of the same heroes and calls it “strategy.” Every victory feels earned, every defeat feels like you’ve just been mugged by RNG itself. The game’s got depth, drama, and enough chaos to make your brain feel like it’s doing calculus on fire. 9/10, would lose another 30-minute match to a guy with a dancing Underlord again.

Very luck based, sometimes you will never get anything you need to win. To much % chances at getting good units that can make big differences. But if you re-roll 6 times and only get nature units when doing a beast build, its like.... what are you even suppose to do? 

Plus there isnt a like unit roster to read what all the units do. You cant pre go learn things, just hope 15 ish seconds is fast enough to read multiple units long paragraph descriptions only after hovering.

Meh, fun but bad game design. At least add a unit list to read through

🎯 Rating: 7.5/10

📜 Overview
Dota Underlords is an auto-battler strategy game developed by Valve, set in the Dota 2 universe. In the game, players recruit units, position them on a grid, and watch them battle automatically against opponents in a series of rounds. With a variety of heroes, items, and strategic synergies, Dota Underlords provides a deep, tactical experience. Though the game has a strong foundation with its Dota 2 ties, it struggles with balancing, occasional pacing issues, and player retention.

🌟 Pros
✅ Deep Strategic Gameplay: Synergies, item choices, and unit placement offer a variety of strategic options.
✅ Connection to Dota 2: Familiar heroes and mechanics for Dota 2 fans, adding a layer of depth.
✅ Variety of Heroes: A wide selection of units and combinations to experiment with.
✅ Regular Updates: Valve’s commitment to balancing and introducing new content.
✅ Offline Play: Single-player mode allows players to enjoy the game without an internet connection.

⚠️ Cons
❌ Pacing Issues: Matches can feel slow, especially early on, which may frustrate some players.
❌ Overly Complex for Newcomers: The steep learning curve makes it difficult for new players to jump in.
❌ Balancing Problems: Some synergies and heroes can be overpowered or underwhelming, leading to a lack of variety.
❌ Monetization: The in-game purchases for cosmetics may detract from the experience for some players.
❌ Player Retention: The game struggles to keep players engaged over the long term, with a repetitive nature.

💬 Player Sentiment
Positive Reviews: Players enjoy the depth of strategy, the tie-ins to the Dota 2 universe, and the variety of tactics available. The regular updates and new heroes keep the game fresh for many.

Negative Reviews: Common criticisms include the pacing issues, steep learning curve, and some balancing problems that make the game feel frustrating at times.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that matches can feel heavily dependent on RNG and luck when waiting for specific heroes to roll and upgrade.

citations.review_text: The rng factor is so stupid. I am waiting on my heroes to come up so I can upgrade to tier 3 and I am waiting and I am waiting. To no avail. Worst game created.

It's supposed to be a casual game, so we can forgive the RNG making this mostly a game of luck. The skill aspect to the game is mainly managing your gold, deciding when to let your loot carry interest or force it to by selling heroes, etc.

This would all be fine, but the game is completely unbalanced time-wise. First of all, let me point out that each match seems to be instantly decided, and we're just watching animations play out. So time is the first imbalance you'll notice, spending most of it waiting in this animation phase where your actions are limited; you can burn your money by re-rolling the RNG-selected hero draft pool, and move pieces around. 

The second waiting period is the important one, and this is the skill aspect of the game. You have to rapidly, very rapidly, do mental arithmetic where you keep a running balance of what would happen if you buy or sell any given hero given your purchase or upgrade options. You have [b][i]less[/i][/b] time in this phase than you do in the Battle Chess-style animation purgatory.

One aspect that cannot be considered skill is the positioning your heroes. This is extremely important, because by default your heroes will not attack the enemy with the lowest HP. So you'll have to position your heroes in such a way that they act in both offensive and defensive synergy.

The reason positioning isn't a skill is because you can only learn how to do this after dozens of games, as there's no way to know the modus operandi of the characters without putting them on the board and seeing how they behave. Even wild animals with wildly low brain-to-bodys ize ratios know to go after the weak, so I bet this is another gem produced by having psychologists involved in game dev: engagement farming the player. You must learn how every hero automatically moves around once the match starts. This is not a skill, it's a way of maximizing your time in game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the developers have abandoned the game and stopped releasing updates or patches.

citations.review_text: This game was and is great, I'm confused as to why Valve put together a team thats spends time to create art, animations, music, etc. To then just push it aside and let it die.

Dota Underlords was a great game and incredibly fun to play, especially with friends. What made it stand out from other auto-battler games was the multiplayer experience. The team modes and ways to play together were amazing, and honestly no other auto-chess style game has come close to the multiplayer features that Dota Underlords had.

Sadly, the game is basically dead now. The last update came out in November 2020, and since then the developers have stopped updating it. Because of that, the meta never changes anymore and a few builds ended up being overpowered. Back when the game was still supported, updates would regularly change the meta and keep things fresh.

Nowadays almost nobody plays it anymore, which is really a shame. I honestly miss the game and the fun matches I had with friends.

If the developers ever decide to update it again and bring it back to life, I would definitely recommend it.
It's a great game. It is just a shame Valve abandoned it. Maybe one day they will bring it back to life. One can dream.

Really love spending some time in this game even in 2026.... The fact that there are still active players after years without new content nor even patches tells for itself. Would love at least some updates from time to time though...

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that multiple players can end up contesting the same starter builds in matches due to game design issues.

citations.review_text:
I achieved everything possible in this game, including reaching Lord of White Spire in both game modes multiple times, completing City Crawl 6 times and killing round 50 Roshan (older patch).

The most frustrating thing about Underlords is having multiple people presented with the same starter builds. There are over 20 viable builds but 2-4 people pick the same one in almost every single game... It's bad design, game should hide already chosen builds on reroll or offer more balanced Knockout packages. Other than that it's a very good card game to which I come back to now and then. I'm chasing that 3star Wraith King high until quitting again because of the build duplication frustration. 
It's a shame they discontinued developing it :(

Autochess is a bit more "build friendly" this game I can play aiming to build something and NEVER see one specific character, I was top 100 in the US in autochess back in 2020. This game is good and deserves all the auto battler praise. I've dabbled here n there, but found it hard lately to find a game? I hope this game thrives.
